newsitem.title: USA: Orange County, N.C., plans $40 mln GO referendum.
newsitem.headline: Orange County, N.C., plans $40 mln GO referendum.

text.p: North Carolina's Orange County tentatively plans a $40 million general obligation bond referendum for schools in November 1997, Assistant County Manager Rod Visser said Thursday.
"That is not set in stone at this particular point," Visser said.

The school financing plan would help the fast-growing county build new schools to keep up with its burgeoning student population. But the plan may have to be re-drawn if voters reject a statewide $1.8 billion general obligation bond issue for schools in the Nov 5 election this year.
"If that state bond issue doesn't pass this year, I believe the commissioners would go back to the drawing board," Visser said.

The statewide bond issue would give the county additional funds for school construction under a matching formula based on ability to pay, student population and enrollment growth rate. Orange County, one of the state's more affluent counties, would have to have raised at least $2.76 locally for school construction over the last four years for each dollar it would receive from the statewide bond issue.
"Orange County spends so much money locally that we really would have no toruble meeting the matching requirement," Visser said.

Orange County voters approved a $22 million school bond referendum in 1988 and a $52 million school bond referendum in 1992. Visser said county commissioners expect to make a final decision on the 1997 school bond referendum in July or August.
